explainer.lead: The post-Adam assortment of optimizers: sign-based updates with tiny memory (Lion), curvature estimates for faster LLM pretraining (Sophia), full second-order preconditioning matrices (Shampoo, SOAP), and memory-lean factorized states (Adafactor). It matters because, together with Muon, it shows optimizer research reopening after a decade of AdamW.

tiers.eli5: For years everyone used the same recipe for training AI models; now a whole shelf of new recipes has appeared, each saving memory or speeding things up in a different way.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pick from the zoo when memory or pretraining speed binds — Lion for a tiny memory footprint, Adafactor for factorized states, Shampoo or SOAP when full second-order preconditioning is affordable. The pitfall is assuming one choice transfers across models and scales.
tiers.paperLevel: The optimizers differ in what they store and apply: sign-based updates with minimal state (Lion), curvature estimates (Sophia), full second-order preconditioning matrices (Shampoo, SOAP), and factorized state (Adafactor). No claim is made here about which wins universally; the evidence is that research reopened after a decade of AdamW.

explainer.example: Pretraining a large language model, a team short on accelerator memory substitutes a factorized-state or sign-based optimizer for AdamW to cut stored state.
